clue.text: Wild cat is stalking cobra, writhing and tumbling

indicators.note: a stalker follows behind its prey, so the cat letters come after the cobra letters
something writhing twists about, so the letters of cobra are twisted into a new order
wild here means out of control, so the letters of cat is are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wild cat hunts a writhing cobra, and both roll about in the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' turns COBRA into ACROB and 'Wild' turns CAT IS into ATICS; 'stalking' puts the cat piece behind the cobra piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbling is a gymnastic display of flips and rolls, the stuff of a circus performer's routine.

clue.text: Handy to be associated with this force?

definitions.text: Handy to be associated with this force?

parts.words: Handy to be associated with this force?
parts.note: a handy item is one with a hand in it; by the same pattern, a word built from limb plus Y would be linked to a military force

explanation.surface: A question about whether it would be useful to join some fighting force.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Handy' as hand + Y; the force in question is the limb one step up from the hand, plus the same Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A land fighting force is the most familiar military body, and its name splits into a limb and a Y.

clue.text: Regret keeping left, leading to blooming ban

indicators.note: the first piece comes before, leading on to, the blooming word
the regret word keeps, or holds, the left letter within it

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a rule that leads to a ban on flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or prohibit something is to bar it, the phrasal-verb sense of ban.

clue.text: Smashing things made from flour mix using metric weights

parts.note: batter is a mixture of flour, eggs and milk
in as in 'written in ink', meaning by means of
grams are units of weight in the metric system

explanation.surface: A recipe: something smashing made from a flour mix, weighed out in metric units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' suggests something delightful in a recipe, but it means things that literally smash.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy beams once swung against castle gates and walls were siege engines built to smash them down.

clue.text: Dream to be 25 with a piercing, instead of old and posh

indicators.note: the a goes into the gap, piercing the word
the a takes the place of the old and posh letters

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, meaning best or thrash
U stands for upper class, hence posh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreamer imagines getting a piercing to look less old-fashioned and grand.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the answer to 25 across, remove O (old) and U (posh), and put A into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dreamlike, half-conscious state, so the noun dream fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Cases found in taxi this person catches

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
the setter speaking of themself is I
nets as a verb means catches, as with fish

explanation.surface: Luggage cases left in a taxi are picked up by the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Display cabinets and cupboards are cases in the furniture sense, boxes for storing or showing things.

clue.text: Men seeking stable parts of moat, grit falling unevenly

indicators.note: only some letters of the words are used
the odd-numbered, uneven, positions are the ones picked out

explanation.surface: A castle siege scene with grit tumbling into the moat.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of 'moat grit' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men of the Nativity story followed a star to the stable in Bethlehem.

clue.text: Husband permitted to wear tucked in jumper?

indicators.note: the eating word wears, or wraps round, the husband and permitted letters

parts.note: to tuck in is to eat heartily, so tucked in means ate
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A husband allowed to wear a jumper tucked into his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater, but it means a sports competitor who jumps, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper or long jumper is one kind of sportsperson in track and field.

clue.text: Voracious, taking a bite of reel bait as nibbling's on the rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
only a bite, a portion, of the run of words is taken

explanation.surface: A greedy fish nibbles the bait on an angler's reel as it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone voracious has an appetite that can never be satisfied, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Motorway with illuminations, westbound excellent for emergency service?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
lit means lights or lighting, as in a lit-up display

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: Motorway signs and lights warn of an emergency vehicle heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a London to Yorkshire motorway. 'emergency service' is a pun: a citizen force called up only when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve force of civilians called up in a crisis gives military service only in emergencies.

clue.text: Boozer in almost entirely prime colours

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the word is used almost whole, dropping its last letter

parts.note: prime means best, as in prime cuts
a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker sitting in a pub painted almost entirely in primary colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LUSH inside BES (best without its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: To go red in the face from embarrassment is to colour up, the verb sense of colours.

clue.text: NY-based organisation shortly becoming French one?

definitions.text: NY-based organisation shortly becoming French one?

parts.words: NY-based organisation shortly becoming French one?
parts.note: the world body based in New York is shortened to two letters, which spell the French word for one

explanation.surface: A New York organisation is about to turn French.
explanation.definitionFit: The international peacekeeping body has its headquarters in Manhattan and is abbreviated to UN, which is also French for one.

clue.text: Rash of surplus plastic noticed around northern France

parts.note: over means extra or left over

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the northern and France letters
plastic means mouldable, so the letters of noticed are remoulded

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Someone spotted surplus plastic around the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far too sure of oneself leads to reckless, rash behaviour; the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Second-rate highway outlaws seizing English food

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second-rate
a highway is a road

indicators.note: the outlaws word seizes, or grips, the English letter

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Highwaymen on a poor road seize an Englishman's food.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flat pale-green beans are a common vegetable, so they are an example of food.

clue.text: Hawk about to face dog

indicators.note: the about word faces, sitting in front of, the dog word

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to dog someone is to follow, or tail, them

explanation.surface: A hawk turns round to face a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning to peddle goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk wares is to sell them, and selling to the public is the shop trade.

clue.text: And what have you from Rome?

definitions.text: And what have you from Rome?

parts.words: And what have you from Rome?
parts.note: the phrase 'and what have you' means 'and so on', and the Romans' Latin gives the stock form of that phrase

explanation.surface: Someone asks what else was brought back from a trip to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag meaning 'and the rest' is the formal equivalent of 'and what have you'.

clue.text: Northern resident declared showers overpriced

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: showers are rain; overpriced means dear

explanation.surface: A northerner complains that showers cost too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern resident' sounds like a person, but it is an Arctic animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlered deer live in Lapland and the Arctic, so they are residents of the far north.

clue.text: Journalist showing behind while notice is given

indicators.note: the journalist shows up behind, placed at the end after the other pieces

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as we spoke'
a sign is a notice
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist turns their back while a notice is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like the rear end, but it is part of the instruction placing ED last.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is allocated to someone has been handed or given to them.

clue.text: Top of singles 100 chart, composed score

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of chart are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A composer writes a score that tops the singles chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical but means to mark a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to mark it with a line, the same as to scrape a mark into it.

clue.text: Weep as son rejected the wine in Provence

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the French words are turned round

parts.note: in French, the wine is le vin

explanation.surface: A son weeps as the local wine in Provence is turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To whimper and cry in a self-pitying way is to weep, in a less dignified form.

clue.text: Home extension also gripped by unruly rave

indicators.note: the also word is held inside the rearranged letters
unruly means disorderly, so the letters of rave are disordered

parts.note: and means also or as well

explanation.surface: A noisy rave spills out of a house's new extension.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed porch built along the side of a house is an extension to the home.

clue.text: Qualified in a tie too, presumably

definitions.meaning: fit or right for something, as in well matched to a job
someone wearing a tie is probably also wearing a jacket and trousers to match

explanation.surface: A qualified person probably also turns up in a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apt for a role and dressed in a matching jacket and trousers share one adjective.

clue.text: A good deal securer using local net search about retiring

parts.note: a local is a pub, also called a bar
a net gain is the profit left over
a hunt is a search

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the about word is turned backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone after a good deal searches the local net shops before retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub. 'A good deal' means a bargain, not 'much'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper who sets out to secure bargains is one who goes after cheap deals.

clue.text: Picked up learned group of 16?

indicators.note: picked up means caught by ear, so the word is heard not read

parts.note: to have heard news is to have learned it

explanation.surface: Someone picked up something learned about a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the answer to 16 down, an Arctic deer, and a group of them is a herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of grazing animals such as deer is called a herd.

clue.text: Quintet sit rabbiting about incorporating singer?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters run backwards
the run of words incorporates, or contains, the letters

explanation.surface: A five-piece band sits chattering about taking on a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbiting' is British slang for chattering on.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer is a performer on stage, an example of the term.

clue.text: Best essence of citrus, small amount

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central part

parts.note: an ounce is a small amount, as in 'not an ounce of sense'

explanation.surface: A recipe calling for a small measure of citrus essence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat them, and to beat thoroughly is to thrash.

clue.text: Get away with late arrival of husband, being somewhere in London

indicators.note: the husband letter arrives later, moving further along the word

parts.note: shoo is the cry used to drive something away

explanation.surface: Someone gets away with a husband turning up late in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London known for nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, so it is one place in the capital.

clue.text: British disarmed revolts, including one person holding up train

indicators.note: the rearranged letters include the one letter
revolts means turns over, so the letters of disarmed are turned about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Disarmed British soldiers revolt, including one who holds up a train in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up train' suggests a robbery; it is a wedding dress train held by an attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's attendant carries the long train of the wedding dress off the ground.
